items.review_rationale: Read the global Cohen–Macaulay condition and identified the Noetherian ring, every prime localization, and the Cohen–Macaulay local-ring predicate. Distinguished prime testing from the equivalent maximal testing formulation.

references.context: Ideal maximal among the proper ideals of R, as an alternative locality test to all prime ideals

references.phrase: for every maximal or prime ideal
references.disposition: Prime-local and maximal-local characterizations are alternative equivalent testing scopes for a Noetherian ring, not a disjunction allowing one chosen prime.

items.review_rationale: Read the patch-topology subbasis construction on a spectral space, including both original quasi-compact opens and their complements, while distinguishing the generated topology from the original one.

references.phrase: ambient topological space and its original topology

references.context: Set complements taken within X, included as new subbasic opens for the constructible topology although they need not be open in the original topology
Smallest topology on the same underlying set containing every original quasi-compact open subset and its complement

references.disposition: The combined family forms a subbasis for the newly generated patch topology; it is not claimed to be a basis or a subbasis for the original spectral topology.

items.review_rationale: Read the continuous map between two spectral spaces and the specific quasi-compact-open inverse-image preservation property. The general quasicompact map definition has this same predicate but not the spectral domain and codomain requirements.

references.phrase: inverse image of each quasi-compact open subset
references.context: Set-theoretic preimage f^{-1}(U), required quasi-compact in X; the openness of this preimage follows from continuity

references.phrase: spectral map versus general quasi-compact map
references.disposition: The inverse-image criterion is reused; being a spectral map additionally assumes spectral spaces on both sides.

items.review_rationale: Read all four defining conditions for a spectral space: sobriety, quasi-compactness, stability of quasi-compact opens under binary intersection, and their basis property. Sobriety was not confused with Hausdorffness.

references.context: Every irreducible nonempty closed subset has a unique generic point; sobriety is separate from Hausdorffness

references.phrase: binary intersections of quasi-compact open sets remain quasi-compact
references.context: Coherence/finiteness condition imposed on the family of quasi-compact opens, not arbitrary quasi-compact subsets

references.disposition: Every original open can be expressed as a union of quasi-compact opens, not necessarily as one quasi-compact open.
